record.paper_title: Open problems on billiards and geometric optics
record.original_question: Suppose an oval has the property that each generic caustic by reflection from an interior light source has exactly four cusps. Does this property characterize ellipses among ovals?

evidence.quote: Question 2: Does the above property characterize ellipses?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let C ⊂ ℝ² be an oval, i.e., a smooth, closed, strictly convex plane curve. Given an interior point O of C ("light source"), consider light rays emanating from O, reflecting off C according to the law of equal angles (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection). For each integer n ≥ 1, the n-th caustic by reflection from O is the envelope of the family of rays obtained after n reflections from C. It is known that for a generic oval C and a generic interior point O, each such caustic is a piecewise smooth curve whose singular points are cusps, and that the number of cusps is at least four.

Suppose that an oval C has the following property: for every n ≥ 1 and for every generic interior light source O, the n-th caustic by reflection from O has exactly four cusps. (Ellipses are known to satisfy this property when O is any non-focal interior point.)

Question: Does this property characterize ellipses? That is, must such an oval C be an ellipse?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work by Bor and Tabachnikov established the lower bound (at least four cusps for generic point sources in any oval) and showed that if an oval is not an ellipse then there exists some n ≥ 1 and an open set of interior points O for which the n-th caustic by reflection has more than four cusps. This provides strong support for the characterization but, together with subsequent work on the ellipse case (Bor–Spivakovsky, 2024), the full converse characterization of ellipses by the exactly-four-cusps property has not been completely settled in published form.

status_evidence.title: On cusps of caustics by reflection: a billiard variation on Jacobi's Last Geometric Statement
status_evidence.snippet: We show that each of these caustics, for a generic point light source, has at least 4 cusps.
status_evidence.claim: Lower bound of four cusps established for generic light sources in ovals; partial progress toward the characterization.

status_evidence.title: Cusps of caustics by reflection in ellipses
status_evidence.snippet: Proves the conjecture for circular billiards; for ellipses describes the location of four cusps but does not show these are the only ones.
status_evidence.claim: Ellipse side of the conjecture only partially established; converse characterization not addressed.
